You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station T-32, survey area T. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 184.7 | 18.51 | 18.51
2 | 735.3 | 0.77 | 19.28
3 | 503.9 | 2.27 | 21.55
4 | 56.6 | 33.69 | 55.24
5 | 43.3 | 5.90 | 61.14
6 | 520.0 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as KQQH-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station T-32, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

Station T-32 (Survey Area T) comprises a six-layer sequence. The resistivity starts at 184.7 ohm-m (Layer 1), increases to 735.3 ohm-m (Layer 2), then decreases through Layers 3 (503.9 ohm-m) and 4 (56.6 ohm-m) to 43.3 ohm-m in Layer 5. Layer 6 increases to 520.0 ohm-m. The curve-type notation for this sequence is KQQH, derived from the consecutive transitions: K (Layers 1-2-3: 184.7 < 735.3 > 503.9), Q (Layers 2-3-4: 735.3 > 503.9 > 56.6), Q (Layers 3-4-5: 503.9 > 56.6 > 43.3), and H (Layers 4-5-6: 56.6 > 43.3 < 520.0). This matches the classification currently on file.
